reader_notes: The essay voice is convincing and the central idea (a saved stomme is an instruction, so the form persists without anyone deciding anything) is carried cleanly by the Rossmåla example, where the skeleton was kept but the lövning was re-laid twice.

q2 option B (the stomme as a 'minnesstöd' for raising and lövning) is the near-miss I had to argue myself out of: the text says the lövning changed even where the stomme was saved, and that nobody needed to remember anything at all. D is the better fit, but B is where a hurried reader lands.
Skarpbo is set up in the opening trio of villages and then never returns; a small loose end in an otherwise tight piece.
1961–1974 is correctly described later as 'de fjorton somrarna' — the dates check out.
